title: Normalized continuous finite-field coefficient presentations
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ any scheme. Equip the native abelian coefficient ring $B_X$ of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data] with its existing commutative monoid structure. For every finite coefficient field $E$ in the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the size transport and specified embedding of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data], there is a CoefficientPresentation: its integral comparison identifies continuous integral functions with the completed constant residue tower, its finite comparisons fix constants and recover pointwise residues, and its integral localization and inclusions have their specified pointwise normalizations. These presentations can be chosen simultaneously so that for $E\le L$ the completed coefficient map followed by the $L$ integral map into $B_X$ equals the $E$ integral map.

proof.text: Use continuousCoefficientCompletion for each finite field. Identify its commutative-ring inverse limit with the existing completion: the finite quotient diagrams agree after forgetting commutativity, this fully faithful forgetful functor preserves limits, and the resulting comparison preserves every projection. Compose the normalized continuous completion isomorphism with this comparison and retain the supplied constant and residue equations.

Use continuousCoefficientLocalization and integralRationalCoefficientMap for the normalized localization and integral inclusion. The specified finite-field embedding is an isometry by uniqueness of the absolute value extending the p-adic norm. Its postcomposition on continuous functions has finite-dimensional span contained in the range of the finite-dimensional source, so it lands in native locally finite functions. The proved section-ring multiplication comparison in NativeScalarForgetting identifies native multiplication with pointwise multiplication; the native unit is pointwise one by applying one_mul to the constant-one function. Thus postcomposition is an actual ring-sheaf morphism with the required pointwise normalization.

For any two normalized presentations, the finite comparison is forced by its values on the sheafification unit, hence is the canonical constant-functions comparison. Its naturality for the existing quotient inclusion maps makes the continuous integral scalar map commute with every reduction. The same-index quotient maps exist for all finite embeddings: integralScalar_quotient_kernel proves this even for ramification. The unique completed coefficient map with those projections is therefore conjugate to continuous integral postcomposition through the two integral isomorphisms. Compose with the normalized integral and native inclusions. Pointwise equality follows from composition of the field embeddings. Choose the presentations simultaneously in the final theorem; cancellation of Shrink.algEquiv and its inverse proves the required embedding equation. The argument needs no points of the site objects and includes empty objects and identity inclusions.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1)--(2), implemented from the existing normalized completion and localization theorems; scalar compatibility by uniqueness of completedCoefficientMap and naturality of the constant-functions comparisons.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientPresentations_exists
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsCommMonObj (abRing l X)] :
    ∃ coefficient : ∀ E : Index l (PadicAlgCl l),
      CoefficientPresentation l X (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) (embedding l E),
      ∀ (E L : Index l (PadicAlgCl l)) (h : E ≤ L),
        completedCoefficientMap l (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E)
            (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) L)
            (coefficientInclusion l (PadicAlgCl l) E L h) X ≫
          (coefficient L).integralMap l X = (coefficient E).integralMap l X
